hints.title: Smashing Cancellation Discrepancy Obstacle
hints.text: Smashing pairs of stones until at most one remains is equivalent to assigning each stone a '+' or '-' sign. How can partitioning stones into two subsets of near-equal weight minimize their remaining difference?

hints.title: Half-Capacity Subset Invariant
hints.text: Finding a subset of stones whose weight sum is as close to total // 2 as possible minimizes total - 2 * sum(S).

hints.title: Boolean Knapsack Reverse Sweep Procedure
hints.text: Compute total weight sum and set target = total // 2. Maintain a boolean array of size target + 1 with entry 0 set to true. For each stone weight w, iterate backward from target down to w: if entry j - w is reachable, mark entry j as reachable. Find the largest reachable index and return total - 2 * index.

hints.title: Complete Implementation

variables: S: half of total stone weight (sum / 2)
complexity.notes: Boolean 1D knapsack checks reachability up to target S.
complexity.whyNaiveFails: Simulating all collision permutations takes exponential time.
complexity.spaceTimeTradeoff: Boolean array of size S + 1 uses minimal memory for S <= 1500.
complexity.interviewerExpectation: Formulating pairwise cancellation as partitioning stones into two balanced subsets.
